title: Choose the visual world for the dashboard
question: The roll assigned the Obeya Wall. Keep it, take the alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Obeya Wall
options.lineage: Toyota obeya rooms and the kanban walls program teams stand at every morning
options.thesis: Every open PR is a card on one wall, racked in the column of whoever moves next; the fullest cells are the bottleneck.
options.viewport: The wall itself: five whose-move columns across, the biggest SIG lanes down, each cell a stack of cards sized by PR count; the top three queues carry numbered red magnets and the finding is written in marker above.
options.risk: Kanban boards are everywhere; set timidly it reads as a generic task board, and cards must stay PRs, never people.

raised.raise: Measured facts in solid ink, proxies in hairline: the wall marks where labels only approximate whose move it is.
Card state is carried by form (pinned, curled, struck), never by colour alone.
On-hold PRs hang visibly in a parked bin under the wall, counted, not hidden.
Red is spent on one thing only: the ranked bottleneck magnets.
Every mark on the wall is data; nothing is decoration.

options.label: Value Stream Map
options.lineage: Lean value stream mapping (Rother & Shook, Learning to See)
options.thesis: Kubernetes review drawn as a value stream: process boxes, triangles of waiting PRs, and a lead-time ladder showing the wait is almost all of it.
options.viewport: The whole stream across the first viewport: ready, first response, lgtm, approved, merged as process boxes, a triangle of waiting PRs between each, and the ladder beneath splitting 7.3 days into waiting versus moving.
options.risk: TPMs know this notation, but others may read it as a flowchart; it is also where most process-analysis pages land.

options.label: Provenance Ribbon
options.thesis: A PR's life as one custody ribbon passing between author, reviewers and approvers, with gaps where it waited.
options.viewport: One ribbon per ranked queue, unrolled across time.
options.case: Fuses well for a single PR's journey but not for ranking queues; hiring managers don't recognize museum custody records.
options.risk: Beautiful for one PR, unclear for 1,270.

options.label: Emission-Line Rail
options.thesis: Every queue a hairline on one wait-time rail, state carried by dash and height.
options.viewport: One rail of wait time with each queue as a line at its median.
options.case: A strong instrument, but neither audience reads spectra, and ranking queues gets harder, not easier.
options.kept: State by form, never colour alone.

options.label: Cutting-Bench Rail
options.thesis: PRs as frames on a perforated rail, set-aside work hanging on pins below.
options.viewport: A frame strip of queues with parked PRs on pins.
options.case: Fuses loosely; film editing isn't the audience's ritual, and the orange field fights the data.
options.kept: Parked work stays visible below the rail.

options.label: Civic Bureau Prospectus
options.thesis: A bone-white plate with all colour spent on one ribbon.
options.viewport: A marketing hero with the finding as headline.
options.case: This is the marketing look the brief rules out; it sells instead of shows.
options.kept: All colour spent on one thing.

options.label: Tanaka Plane Portrait
options.thesis: The finding built from a few flat planes of colour on a quiet grid.
options.viewport: A poster of queue planes sized by PR-days.
options.case: Striking, but it trades the drill-down for a poster; proof gets harder.

options.label: Curved-Crease Shell
options.thesis: One sweeping crease gives the page its structure.
options.viewport: The flow of review drawn as one folded arc.
options.case: No route from paper engineering to PR queues for either audience.
options.kept: One governing line organises the page.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: An engineering-metrics dashboard: KPI tiles, bar charts and a sortable table, executed cleanly.
canonCard.viewport: Headline tiles, then the brief, the ranked table and the charts, as the page looks today.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every analytics product by design.
